newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GREENPEACE BLOCKS BORSSELE NUCLEAR WASTE TRANSPORT.
newsitem.headline: GREENPEACE BLOCKS BORSSELE NUCLEAR WASTE TRANSPORT.

text.p: Twelve protestors from environmental lobby group Greenpeace on Tuesday blocked the transport of nuclear waste from the Borssele nuclear power plant in southern Netherlands.

"We're blocking a nuclear transport (shipment) from Borselle to La Hague (in northern France)....as it is totally unsafe. Such reprocessing is also uneconomical," said Greenpeace spokesman Rene Danen.
The plant manager at Borselle Johannis den Boer confirmed the Greenpeace action but said the radiation risks were almost zero and that the case for reprocessing was sound.

"It's absolutely safe for the people in the surrounding area. The radiation is millions of times below the acceptable international level.... If we had to change our policy, it would only lead to an increase in the price of electricity," he said.

EPZ (Elektriciteits-Produktiemaatschaapij Zuid-Nederland) which owns and operates the Dutch plant was exporting the nuclear waste to the La Hague nuclear station for reprocessing. The French authorities are under contract to encase the reprocessed waste in glass and return it to EPZ from the year 2000 for storage.
Greenpeace said it had sent a letter to 30,000 residents near the Borselle plant to inform them of the regular passage of nuclear waste along local roads.
The action continued, about 500 metres from the plant gates, as police arrived, Greenpeace said.
"We will continue (the protest) until the police end it or until the radiation gets too high (for the protestors)," said spokesman Danen.
Following the closure of the small experimental Dodewaard station next year, the 449 MW (megawatt) Borselle plant will be only remaining nuclear power station in the Netherlans.
